newsitem.title: FRANCE: PRESS DIGEST - FRANCE - LE MONDE JUNE 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - FRANCE - LE MONDE JUNE 27.

text.p: These are leading stories in afternoon daily Le Monde.

-- Prime Minister Lionel Jospin sends budget instruction letter to ministers highlighting employment as the "absolute priority" but stating this must be done at the same time as launching European monetary union on schedule.
Jospin tells ministers they must live up to election
promises within confines of the credits attributed to them, altering their priorities and questioning commitments of the previous government.
-- France will not limit deficit to three percent of gross domestic product in 1997, according to comments on the budget situation by Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn yesterday.
-- Air France carries on pulling out of its tour operator subsidiaries.
-- Arms manufacturer GIAT Industries authorised not to present 1996 accounts due to uncertainty over its Belgian subsidiary Herstal.

-- Guinness and GrandMet to negotiate with LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault in Paris next week. Arnault is opposed to their merger projects and holds 14.2 percent of Guinness and 6.4 percent of GrandMet.
